To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the face recognition systems can be divided into three categories: (1) template matching and feature measurement; (2) analysis of global and localized facial features; and (3) incorporation of interpersonal and intra-personal variations of human face.

the best face recognition techniques are based on the use of a combination of global and local information and the use of a feature selection mechanism that is able to weigh the information about the facial features together with the localized image features.
the best performance is achieved by combining global and local features, and that the best performance can be achieved by incorporating both intrapersonal and interpersonal variations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of face recognition in still images and video sequences.
the development of a new framework for face recognition systems.
developing an understanding of the internal representation used in face recognition systems, and the implications of this understanding for future research in the field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best face recognition systems are those that incorporate both global and local features, and that are able to adapt to variations within the same class of faces.
there is no single representation that is best for all face recognition systems.
the most promising approach for future development in the field of face recognition systems is a hybrid system which incorporates several techniques from different categories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach to face recognition, which has been successfully applied to a large database of face images.
we have shown that the internal representation of a face recognition system is a key factor in the overall performance of the system.
we have shown how to use the face as a source of information to identify the individual, and we have also demonstrated the feasibility of a face-based biometric identification system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no silver-bullet solutions for face recognition and that a successful face recognition system will likely be a combination of several different approaches.
the current state-of-the-art methods for face recognition are not necessarily the most suitable ones for real world applications.
a face recognition system can be designed in a way that is more robust to changes in facial appearance and more efficient in the use of computational resources.
